meanings: a system of words and grammar that people use to communicate
the words and style used by a particular group or in a particular field

examples.sentence: The report is written in very technical language.

etymology.text: From Old French langage, from langue 'tongue', which comes from Latin lingua; it came into Middle English around 1300.

simple-translation: the words people use to talk and write
the kind of words a group of people use
grammar-teacher: Countable when it means one particular language, as in two languages, but uncountable when it means speech in general, as in the power of language.
It takes in before the name of a language: written in English, never written on English.

core.key: Languages are the bridges connecting people and the world.
meanings: Languages let people understand one another and the wider world, as a bridge joins two places.

examples.sentence: Music is the bridge connecting hearts and cultures.

pronunciation: Languages are the bridges connecting people and the world.
simple-translation: Languages help people understand each other and the world.
grammar-teacher: Languages is plural, so the verb is are.
Connecting people and the world is a participle phrase: it means that connect people and the world.
